newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks slide just lower at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks slide just lower at open.

text.p: Australian shares eased at the opening on Thursday after Wall Street weakened and local bonds softened.
By 10.15 a.m. (2315 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 1.9 points lower at 2,489.1.
The death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping was not affecting trading.
Brokers said the market was set to drift again with minor losses by the end of the day failing to surprise.
The focus remains on individual corporate results with a busy day in prospect for profit releases.
China-related stocks were mixed bag and thinly traded, as usual, after the announcement of Deng's death.
China Construction Holdings Ltd was down two cents at 87 cents (US$0.67) while OLS Asia Holdings Ltd was down one at 81 cents.
However, Jardine Fleming Asia Pacific Ltd was up a cent at 87 cents while NMFM Asia Investments was up a cent at 89 cents.
"It (Deng's death) has not been an issue at our end so far," a Sydney dealer said.
"We are all watching the (corporate) results at the moment," the dealer said. Others agreed.

"Nobody was expecting too much this morning," said dealer Peter Struk of Reynolds and Co. "They did expect metals to be a little better after the LME strength last night, but the rest should have come off and it has slowly eased back."
Shares of Burns Philp and Co fell a cent to A$2.09 after the food ingredients group reported a 17.6 percent rise in first half net profit to A$48.2 million.

Shares of construction group Leighton Holdings fell five cents to A$5.80 despite the company's announcement of an 18 percent rise in first half net profit to A$32.04 million and dividend increase to nine cents per share from 6.5 cents.
Qantas Airways Ltd reported a 2.4 percent higher first half net profit of A$151.6 million.
Its shares were five cents higher at A$2.47.
Falls slightly shaded rises, while about 44 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
